observation: An n-second TWAP of a free-text price description, ending at the expiry. The description is not a reference: what it denotes is a separate reviewed mapping in references/reference-map.json, keyed by the venue's exact text. This entry states the PAYOFF only.

sources.title: Hyperliquid deployer templates: outcomeTemplates, binaryPrice
quotes: resolves to Yes if the {perp} price is above {threshold} at {time}

ambiguities: THE STRIKE IS OWNED BY NEITHER SIDE. The template says the market resolves to Yes if the price is 'above' the threshold, not 'at or above', so at the threshold exactly neither YES nor NO is paid. That differs from the canonical priceBinary, where YES is [K, inf) and the two sides partition the domain. A holder of both sides is paid nothing at exactly one price.

Whether a deployer reads 'above' as strict is not a rule this project can discover: settlement is a submitted fraction (EVIDENCE section 1), so each deployer's reading governs its own settlement. The payoff here is what the TEMPLATE says, and it holds only under the assumption declared above.

The template metadata says 'This market must refer to the price of a Hyperliquid perp', and 42 of 69 live instances name a Pyth series instead. The reference mapping refuses those as ambiguous rather than choosing which text governs.

The `perp` term is frequently not a perp: of 69 instances on 18 September, 23 name BTC and 10 HYPE, while the rest name xyz:GOLD, xyz:SP500, xyz:INTC, xyz:CRCL and others -- equities, indices and commodities. The field name says perp; the values do not.
